record.acip: BZHI DGE SLONG 'CHAR KA LTA BU LA TSANG BA LAS, MGON PO KLU SGRUB LA'ANG DNGOS GNAS PA MTSANG LA, RANG RES KYANG SANGS RGYAS DANG KHYAD MED PA'I BLA MA MJAL TE CHOS GSUNGS PA SOGS KYIS DE DAG DOD THUB SBYOR DU YOD PA LAS DNGOS GNAS MA TSANG YANG , DAL BA BRGYAD DNGOS SU TSANG BA LA GTZO BOR DGONGS TE GSUNGS PA RED,
record.wylie: bzhi dge slong 'char ka lta bu la tshang ba las, mgon po klu sgrub la'ang dngos gnas pa mtshang la, rang res kyang sangs rgyas dang khyad med pa'i bla ma mjal te chos gsungs pa sogs kyis de dag dod thub sbyor du yod pa las dngos gnas ma tshang yang , dal ba brgyad dngos su tshang ba la gtso bor dgongs te gsungs pa red
record.english: All four of the fortunes just explained have been possessed even by the likes of the monk Udayi,43 whereas the same cannot be said even for the Savior Nagarjuna, who lacked them in their literal form. We too have met our Lamas, who are no different from a Buddha, and they have spoken the Dharma and so on; these are a full substitute yes, but we cannot say that we have all those fortunes in their literal form. We do however enjoy all eight of the spiritual leisures; these then are our primary advantage, and it's with this fact in mind that the verse reads "life of leisure."

record.acip: YANG KHA CIG NA RE, NYI SHU PA'I 'GREL BSHAD SLOB DPON DUL BA LHAS MDZAD PA LAS, DE LA RNAG GI THIGS PA 'GA' YANG MED NA RNAG GIS GANG BA'I KLUNG LTA GA LA YOD, LAS KYI RNAM PAR SMIN PA'I DBANG GIS DE DAG GIS DE MTHONG NGO , , ZHES GSUNGS PA DE MI 'THAD PAR THAL, 'GRO BA GSUM GYIS BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA, YI DVAGS KYI MIG SHES TSAD MAR SONG BA'I RNAG DNGOS GNAS PA YOD PA'I PHYIR ZER NA,
record.wylie: yang kha cig na re, nyi shu pa'i 'grel bshad slob dpon dul ba lhas mdzad pa las, de la rnag gi thigs pa 'ga' yang med na rnag gis gang ba'i klung lta ga la yod, las kyi rnam par smin pa'i dbang gis de dag gis de mthong ngo , , zhes gsungs pa de mi 'thad par thal, 'gro ba gsum gyis brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe na, yi dvags kyi mig shes tshad mar song ba'i rnag dngos gnas pa yod pa'i phyir zer na
record.english: Someone might make the following claim: In his Commentary to the Twenty Verses, Master Vinitadeva makes this statement-- If there was not a single drop of pus there, then how could there ever be a whole river of pus? They are forced to see it, through the ripening of their karma. According to you, this statement would have to be mistaken, because when the three different kinds of beings sit down together and look at the glass full of something wet and flowing, the visual consciousness of the craving spirit is a valid perception, and the pus is real pus.

record.acip: DE LTAR MA YIN NA GZUGS LA SOGS PA'I SKYE MCHED RNAMS MED PAR THAL, DE YOD PAR STON PA'I MDO DRANG DON DGONGS PA CAN GYI MDO YIN PA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, NYI SHU PA'I RANG 'GREL LAS, DE BZHIN DU BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYI GZUGS LA SOGS PA'I SKYE MCHED YOD PAR GSUNGS PA YANG DE STON PAS 'DUL BA'I SKYE BO'I CHED DU STE BKA' DE NI DGONGS PA CAN NO, , ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
record.wylie: de ltar ma yin na gzugs la sogs pa'i skye mched rnams med par thal, de yod par ston pa'i mdo drang don dgongs pa can gyi mdo yin pa'i phyir, der thal, nyi shu pa'i rang 'grel las, de bzhin du bcom ldan 'das kyi gzugs la sogs pa'i skye mched yod par gsungs pa yang de ston pas 'dul ba'i skye bo'i ched du ste bka' de ni dgongs pa can no, , zhes gsungs pa'i phyir
record.english: If this were not the case, then one would have to say that form and other such doorways through which perceptions grow do not even exist at all. Why? Because you would be saying that all the sutras which state that they exist are sutras which do not mean what they say; sutras which you have to interpret to understand their true meaning. And this too is certainly the case, for the autocommentary to the Twenty Verses states that: In the same way, statements by the victorious Buddha where He says that form and other such doors of perception do exist would be examples of His word that must be interpreted to establish their real meaning; statements that are only spoken figuratively, for the benefit of disciples who might require such explanations.

record.acip: BYAS PA LA KHO NA RE, SKYON MED DE, PHYI ROL DON DU GRUB PA'I GZUGS SOGS SKYE MCHED YOD PAR STON PA'I MDO DRANG DON DGONGS PA CAN YIN PA'I DON YIN PA'I PHYIR, ZER NA, LUNG SNGA MA'I DON YANG MTSUNGS TE, PHYI ROL DON DU GRUB PA'I RNAG KHRAG GI THIGS PA 'GA' YANG MED CES PA'I DON YIN PA'I PHYIR,
record.wylie: byas pa la kho na re, skyon med de, phyi rol don du grub pa'i gzugs sogs skye mched yod par ston pa'i mdo drang don dgongs pa can yin pa'i don yin pa'i phyir, zer na, lung snga ma'i don yang mtshungs te, phyi rol don du grub pa'i rnag khrag gi thigs pa 'ga' yang med ces pa'i don yin pa'i phyir
record.english: In response to this someone might claim: There's no problem; the point of this statement is to say that sutras which explain form and similar doors of perception as actually existing as outer objects are only spoken figuratively, and must be interpreted to establish their true meaning. Well then, the meaning of the original statement then is just the same: it is saying that "there does not exist even a drop of pus and blood which exists as an outer object."

record.acip: YANG KHA CIG, YI DVAGS KYIS CHU KLUNG LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, CHU KLUNG BSKAMS PA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA'I DE'I MIG SHES DANG , 'BRAS BU CAN GYI LJON PA LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, 'BRAS BU MED PA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA'I DE'I MIG SHES TSAD MA YOD PAR THAL, 'GRO BA GSUM GYIS BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, RNAG KHRAG DNGOS GNAS PA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA'I YI DVAGS KYI MIG SHES TSAD MA YOD PA'I PHYIR,
record.wylie: yang kha cig, yi dvags kyis chu klung la bltas pa de'i tshe, chu klung bskams pa la tshad mar song ba'i de'i mig shes dang , 'bras bu can gyi ljon pa la bltas pa de'i tshe, 'bras bu med pa la tshad mar song ba'i de'i mig shes tshad ma yod par thal, 'gro ba gsum gyis brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la bltas pa de'i tshe, rnag khrag dngos gnas pa la tshad mar song ba'i yi dvags kyi mig shes tshad ma yod pa'i phyir
record.english: Yet again, another argument might be made: Let's take the case of one of those craving spirits that looks at a river of water, and sees it as a dry riverbed, genuinely so. Or consider one that looks at a tree loaded with fruit, but sees it as nothing but bare limbs, genuinely so. The visual consciousness of both of these beings then must be a valid perception. Why? Remember the case of the three different beings looking at a glass full of something wet and flowing; according to you, the pus and blood was actual pus and blood, and the perception of them by the craving spirit was genuine: his visual consciousness was a valid perception.

record.acip: ZER NA MA KHYAB STE, DANG POR YI DVAGS KYIS CHU MA MTHONG NA PHYOGS DER LONGS SPYOD PA'I PHYIR, 'GRO BA YANG MI 'THAD PAS DANG POR CHU MTHONG YANG , PHYIS LAS KYI DBANG GIS CHU MA MTHONG BAR 'OG GZHI GRAM SREG TZAM ZHIG MTHONG ZHING , DE'I RJES SU RTOG PAS CHU BSKAMS PAR ZHEN PA DANG , DE BZHIN DU DANG POR LJON SHING GI 'BRAS BU MTHONG YANG PHYIS LAS KYI DBANG GIS 'BRAS BU MA MTHONG BAR YAL GA TZAM ZHIG MTHONG ZHING , DE'I RJES SU RTOG PAS 'BRAS BU MED PAR ZHEN PA'I PHYIR,
record.wylie: zer na ma khyab ste, dang por yi dvags kyis chu ma mthong na phyogs der longs spyod pa'i phyir, 'gro ba yang mi 'thad pas dang por chu mthong yang , phyis las kyi dbang gis chu ma mthong bar 'og gzhi gram sreg tsam zhig mthong zhing , de'i rjes su rtog pas chu bskams par zhen pa dang , de bzhin du dang por ljon shing gi 'bras bu mthong yang phyis las kyi dbang gis 'bras bu ma mthong bar yal ga tsam zhig mthong zhing , de'i rjes su rtog pas 'bras bu med par zhen pa'i phyir
record.english: Just because we said that about the other case doesn't mean that it's true in every case. If the craving spirit hadn't seen any water in that area in the first place, it wouldn't have made any sense for him to go over in that direction to try to enjoy some of the water. Therefore what happened was that, at first, he saw some water. Later on, he was forced by his karma to stop seeing water and saw only bare, parched earth. Then he had an impression where he thought the water had dried up. The case with the fruit tree is the same. Although at first the craving spirit sees a tree loaded with fruit, later on his karma forces him to stop seeing fruit, and all he sees is bare branches. Then he has an impression where he thinks that the tree has no fruit any more.

record.acip: RNAM PA GCIG TU NA, YI DVAGS KYIS CHU KLUNG LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA DE MA BSKAMS KYANG , RANG GI BLTA BYAR GYUR PA'I CHU KLUNG DANG , LONGS SPYOD BYAR GYUR PA'I CHU KLUNG BSKAMS PA YOD DE, 'GRO BA GSUM GYIS BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA, LAS KYI DBANG GIS RNAG KHRAG SOGS DNGOS PO RNAM PA GSUM CIG CAR DU GRUB PA ZHIG YOD PA'I PHYIR,
record.wylie: rnam pa gcig tu na, yi dvags kyis chu klung la bltas pa de'i tshe na de ma bskams kyang , rang gi blta byar gyur pa'i chu klung dang , longs spyod byar gyur pa'i chu klung bskams pa yod de, 'gro ba gsum gyis brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe na, las kyi dbang gis rnag khrag sogs dngos po rnam pa gsum cig car du grub pa zhig yod pa'i phyir
record.english: From one point of view, the river of water hasn't dried up when the craving spirit looks at it; but there is a river which has dried up, if you're talking about a river of water that the spirit can see, or a river of water that the spirit can drink from. This follows because when the three different types of beings sit down together and look at a glass full of something wet and flowing, it is true that, due to the force of karma, three different kinds of objects exist there at the same time: the pus and blood, and the other two.

record.acip: BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA LHA MI YI DVAGS DUD 'GRO SOGS KYIS CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA, LHA YI BDUD RTZI SNANG BA'I SNANG BA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA DANG , YI DVAGS LA RNAG KHRAG SNANG BA'I SNANG BA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA YOD KYANG , SNANG GZHIR GYUR PA'I RNAG KHRAG SOGS MED NA, SEMS CAN DMYAL BA'I MIG SHES DES, DMYAL BA'I LCAGS SREG DANG , RAL GRI'I NAGS TSAL DANG , ME TSOGS LA SOGS PA SNANG BA'I SNANG BA TZAM LA TSAD MAR SONG BA YOD KYI, DE DAG DNGOS GNAS PA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA MED PAR THAL, KHYOD KYI DAM BCA' 'THAD PA GANG ZHIG, RGYU MTSAN MTSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
record.wylie: brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la lha mi yi dvags dud 'gro sogs kyis cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe na, lha yi bdud rtsi snang ba'i snang ba la tshad mar song ba dang , yi dvags la rnag khrag snang ba'i snang ba la tshad mar song ba yod kyang , snang gzhir gyur pa'i rnag khrag sogs med na, sems can dmyal ba'i mig shes des, dmyal ba'i lcags sreg dang , ral gri'i nags tshal dang , me tshogs la sogs pa snang ba'i snang ba tsam la tshad mar song ba yod kyi, de dag dngos gnas pa la tshad mar song ba med par thal, khyod kyi dam bca' 'thad pa gang zhig, rgyu mtshan mtshungs pa'i phyir
record.english: And consider again this case where a pleasure being and a human and a craving spirit and an animal or the like all sit down together and look at a glass full of something wet and flowing. According to you, it would have to be genuine when something that just looked like ambrosia appeared to the pleasure being, and it would have to be genuine when something that just looked like pus and blood appeared to the craving spirit, but there couldn't be any pus and blood out there to appear as pus and blood. And if this were the case, then consider the visual consciousness of a being in the hells. It would then have to be a valid perception towards something appearing to it that just looked like the burning steel of the hells, and towards something that just looked like the forest of swords, and towards something that just looked like a mass of fire, and so on. Finally, this person would not have any valid perceptions at all towards any of these things as actual objects. Why would this all have to be so? If your idea were correct, it would have to be, for the logic here is identical to your own.

record.acip: 'DOD NA, LCAGS SREG LA SOGS PAS, DER SKYES PA'I 'GRO BA'I LUS SREG PA DANG , GTUB PA LA SOGS PA DNGOS GNAS PA ZHIG MED PAR THAL, 'DOD PA DE'I PHYIR, 'DOD NA, DMYAL BA'I SDUG BSNGAL MED PAR THAL, 'DOD PA DE'I PHYIR, GZHAN YANG DE LTAR CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA, MI'I MIG SHES TSAD MAR SONG BA'I CHU DNGOS GNAS PA MED PAR THAL, DE'I TSE NA RNAG KHRAG DNGOS GNAS PA MED PA'I PHYIR,
record.wylie: 'dod na, lcags sreg la sogs pas, der skyes pa'i 'gro ba'i lus sreg pa dang , gtub pa la sogs pa dngos gnas pa zhig med par thal, 'dod pa de'i phyir, 'dod na, dmyal ba'i sdug bsngal med par thal, 'dod pa de'i phyir, gzhan yang de ltar cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe na, mi'i mig shes tshad mar song ba'i chu dngos gnas pa med par thal, de'i tshe na rnag khrag dngos gnas pa med pa'i phyir
record.english: And suppose you agree that this hell being could have no valid perceptions of the type we mentioned. Well then, the burning steel and other objects could never perform any real actions: they could never burn the bodies of the people born there, they could never chop them up, and so on. Why? Well because of what you just agreed to. And suppose you agree to this; that they could never perform any real actions. Well then, the torment of the hells itself then must not even exist, by your own admission. And remember too that case where the beings all sit down and look at the same thing. You must be saying then that the actual water, the thing towards which the visual consciousness of the human is a valid perception, doesn't exist at all. Why? Well because, according to you, no actual pus and blood exists either in the same situation.

record.acip: KHO NA RE, DE'I TSE NA CHU DNGOS GNAS PA YOD DE, CHUS LUS 'KHRUD PA DANG 'TSOD PAR BYED PA MI RANG GIS MYONG BAS 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR ZER NA, 'O NA, DE'I TSE NA, RNAG KHRAG DNGOS GNAS YOD PAR THAL, DE'I TSE NA, RNAG KHRAG LA LONGS SPYOD PA DANG , LTO BA DANG MGRIN PA LA SOGS PA 'TSIG PA YI DVAGS RANG GIS MYONG BAS 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR,
record.wylie: kho na re, de'i tshe na chu dngos gnas pa yod de, chus lus 'khrud pa dang 'tshod par byed pa mi rang gis myong bas 'grub pa'i phyir zer na, 'o na, de'i tshe na, rnag khrag dngos gnas yod par thal, de'i tshe na, rnag khrag la longs spyod pa dang , lto ba dang mgrin pa la sogs pa 'tshig pa yi dvags rang gis myong bas 'grub pa'i phyir
record.english: Someone might now make the following claim: In this situation, there does exist some real water there. This is because the human can confirm the water with his own experience, as it performs all the functions of water--as he uses it to wash himself, or as he uses it to cook something. Well then, in the same situation there must exist some real pus and blood there as well, because in this same situation the craving spirit can confirm the pus and blood with his own experience as they perform their functions--as he drinks them, and then as the sizzle in his throat and stomach, and so on.

record.acip: BYAS PA LA KHO NA RE, MI LA LUS 'KHRUD PA SOGS DNGOS GNAS PA MED PAR THAL, DE MI RANG GI BLOS RLOM PA TZAM YIN PA'I PHYIR, ZER NA,
record.wylie: byas pa la kho na re, mi la lus 'khrud pa sogs dngos gnas pa med par thal, de mi rang gi blos rlom pa tsam yin pa'i phyir, zer na
record.english: Someone may respond to this with another claim: When the human washes himself with the water and so on, it must not be something real, because it's nothing more than his own imagination.

record.acip: YI DVAGS LA YANG LTO BSREG PA SOGS DNGOS GNAS PA MED PAR THAL, DE YI DVAGS RANG GI BLOS RLOM PA TZAM YIN PA'I PHYIR, 'DOD NA, YI DVAGS KYI SDUG BSNGAL MED PAR THAL,
record.wylie: yi dvags la yang lto bsreg pa sogs dngos gnas pa med par thal, de yi dvags rang gi blos rlom pa tsam yin pa'i phyir, 'dod na, yi dvags kyi sdug bsngal med par thal
record.english: Are you saying then that when the pus and blood sizzle in the stomach of the craving spirit, and so on, it can't be something real? For that too is nothing more than his own imagination. You agree? Well then, the suffering of craving spirits must not exist at all.

record.acip: KHO NA RE, DE LTAR CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA'I TSE, RNAG KHRAG DNGOS GNAS PA MED PAR THAL, RAB RIB CAN GYIS BSE RU LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE BSE RU'I NANG DU SKRA SHAD MED PA GANG ZHIG, RAB RIB DANG LDAN DBANG PO CAN MTSUNGS PA, , CHU 'BAB KLUNG LA YI DVAGS RNAG BLO YANG , , ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR, ZER NA,
record.wylie: kho na re, de ltar cig car du bltas pa'i tshe, rnag khrag dngos gnas pa med par thal, rab rib can gyis bse ru la bltas pa de'i tshe bse ru'i nang du skra shad med pa gang zhig, rab rib dang ldan dbang po can mtshungs pa, , chu 'bab klung la yi dvags rnag blo yang , , zhes gsungs pa'i phyir, zer na
record.english: Someone might make the following claim: Isn't it true that when all those beings sit down together and look at something, there isn't any actual pus and blood at all? Because isn't it true first of all that, when a person with cataracts looks into a porcelain basin, there is no strand of hair in the basin at all? And, secondly, doesn't [Master Dharmakirti's] text itself say, Identical to the case of someone where his sense power has a cataract, Is the mind of a craving spirit as well, which sees a stream of water as pus.

record.wylie: skyon med de, dbu sems gnyis don shes yod med mtshungs mi mtshungs dpyod pa'i skabs yin pa'i phyir dang , yi dvags kyi mig shes la chu klung rnag khrag tu snang ba'i tshe na, de ltar snang ba'i mig shes tshad ma ma yin pa dang , chu klung la bltas pa de'i tshe na, rnag khrag dngos gnas pa zhig yod pa mi 'gal ba'i phyir
record.english: And yet there is no such problem, for this quotation appears in the section where we are examining the question of whether, in the schools of the Middle Way and the Mind-Only, an object and the perception of it must be equivalent in either both existing or both not existing. Moreover, there is another fact about this situation, where the stream of water appears as pus and blood to the visual consciousness of the craving spirit. It is no inconsistency to say that the visual consciousness that sees things this way is not a valid perception, and to say at the same time that--when the craving spirit looks at the stream of water--there does exist there actual pus and blood.

record.english: Someone again may come and claim the following: Let's consider once more this situation where three different types of beings sit down together and look at a glass full of something wet and flowing. Isn't it true that there is no actual pus and blood there? Because isn't it true that the burning steel and so on in the hells is only something that appears to a person who is born there, but that there is nothing there which actually is these objects? Because isn't it true that there is no one at all who went and made all these kinds of things? And isn't this a fact, because doesn't the text of The Bodhisattva's Way of Life say: Who made the burning steel that acts As the floor of the world of hell? Where did all the mass of flames You find there all come from? The Able Ones have spoken that Everything there like this Is nothing at all other than The mind of what's non-virtue.

Because you would be saying that all the sutras which state that they do exist are sutras which do not mean what they say; sutras which you have to interpret to understand their true meaning. And this too is certainly the case, for the autocommentary to the Twenty Verses states that: In the same way, statements by the victorious Buddha where He says that form and other such doors of perception do exist would be examples of His word that must be interpreted to establish their real meaning; statements that are only spoken figuratively, for the benefit of disciples who might require such explanations.

record.acip: BYAS PA LA KHO NA RE, SKYON MED DE, PHYI ROL DON DU GRUB PA'I GZUGS SOGS SKYE MCHED YOD PAR STON PA'I MDO DRANG DON DGONGS PA CAN YIN PA'I DON YIN PA'I PHYIR, ZER NA, LUNG SNGA MA'I DON YANG MTSUNGS TE, PHYI ROL DON DU GRUB PA'I RNAG KHRAG GI THIGS PA 'GA' YANG MED CES PA'I DON YIN PA'I PHYIR,
record.wylie: byas pa la kho na re, skyon med de, phyi rol don du grub pa'i gzugs sogs skye mched yod par ston pa'i mdo drang don dgongs pa can yin pa'i don yin pa'i phyir, zer na, lung snga ma'i don yang mtshungs te, phyi rol don du grub pa'i rnag khrag gi thigs pa 'ga' yang med ces pa'i don yin pa'i phyir
record.english: In response to this someone might claim: There's no problem; the point of this statement is to say that sutras which explain form and similar doors of perception as actually existing as outer objects are only spoken figuratively, and must be interpreted to establish their true meaning. Well then, the meaning of the original statement then is just the same: it is saying that "there does not exist even a drop of pus and blood which exists as an outer object."

record.acip: YANG KHA CIG, YI DVAGS KYIS CHU KLUNG LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, CHU KLUNG BSKAMS PA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA'I DE'I MIG SHES DANG , 'BRAS BU CAN GYI LJON PA LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, 'BRAS BU MED PA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA'I DE'I MIG SHES TSAD MA YOD PAR THAL, 'GRO BA GSUM GYIS BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, RNAG KHRAG DNGOS GNAS PA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA'I YI DVAGS KYI MIG SHES TSAD MA YOD PA'I PHYIR,
record.wylie: yang kha cig, yi dvags kyis chu klung la bltas pa de'i tshe, chu klung bskams pa la tshad mar song ba'i de'i mig shes dang , 'bras bu can gyi ljon pa la bltas pa de'i tshe, 'bras bu med pa la tshad mar song ba'i de'i mig shes tshad ma yod par thal, 'gro ba gsum gyis brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la bltas pa de'i tshe, rnag khrag dngos gnas pa la tshad mar song ba'i yi dvags kyi mig shes tshad ma yod pa'i phyir
record.english: Yet again, another argument might be made: Let's take the case of one of those craving spirits that looks at a river of water, and sees it as a dry riverbed, genuinely so. Or consider one that looks at a tree loaded with fruit, but sees it as nothing but bare limbs, genuinely so. The visual consciousness of both of these beings then must be a valid perception. Why? Remember the case of the three different beings looking at a glass full of something wet and flowing; according to you, the pus and blood was actual pus and blood, and the perception of them by the craving spirit was genuine: his visual consciousness was a valid perception.

record.acip: ZER NA MA KHYAB STE, DANG POR YI DVAGS KYIS CHU MA MTHONG NA PHYOGS DER LONGS SPYOD PA'I PHYIR, 'GRO BA YANG MI 'THAD PAS DANG POR CHU MTHONG YANG , PHYIS LAS KYI DBANG GIS CHU MA MTHONG BAR 'OG GZHI GRAM SREG TZAM ZHIG MTHONG ZHING , DE'I RJES SU RTOG PAS CHU BSKAMS PAR ZHEN PA DANG , DE BZHIN DU DANG POR LJON SHING GI 'BRAS BU MTHONG YANG PHYIS LAS KYI DBANG GIS 'BRAS BU MA MTHONG BAR YAL GA TZAM ZHIG MTHONG ZHING , DE'I RJES SU RTOG PAS 'BRAS BU MED PAR ZHEN PA'I PHYIR,
record.wylie: zer na ma khyab ste, dang por yi dvags kyis chu ma mthong na phyogs der longs spyod pa'i phyir, 'gro ba yang mi 'thad pas dang por chu mthong yang , phyis las kyi dbang gis chu ma mthong bar 'og gzhi gram sreg tsam zhig mthong zhing , de'i rjes su rtog pas chu bskams par zhen pa dang , de bzhin du dang por ljon shing gi 'bras bu mthong yang phyis las kyi dbang gis 'bras bu ma mthong bar yal ga tsam zhig mthong zhing , de'i rjes su rtog pas 'bras bu med par zhen pa'i phyir
record.english: Just because we said that about the other case doesn't mean that it's true in every case. If the craving spirit hadn't seen any water in that area in the first place, it wouldn't have made any sense for him to go over in that direction to try to enjoy some of the water. Therefore what happened was that, at first, he saw some water. Later on, he was forced by his karma to stop seeing water and saw only bare, parched earth. Then he had an impression where he thought the water had dried up. The case with the fruit tree is the same. Although at first the craving spirit sees a tree loaded with fruit, later on his karma forces him to stop seeing fruit, and all he sees is bare branches. Then he has an impression where he thinks that the tree has no fruit any more.

record.acip: RNAM PA GCIG TU NA, YI DVAGS KYIS CHU KLUNG LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA DE MA BSKAMS KYANG , RANG GI BLTA BYAR GYUR PA'I CHU KLUNG DANG , LONGS SPYOD BYAR GYUR PA'I CHU KLUNG BSKAMS PA YOD DE, 'GRO BA GSUM GYIS BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA, LAS KYI DBANG GIS RNAG KHRAG SOGS DNGOS PO RNAM PA GSUM CIG CAR DU GRUB PA ZHIG YOD PA'I PHYIR,
record.wylie: rnam pa gcig tu na, yi dvags kyis chu klung la bltas pa de'i tshe na de ma bskams kyang , rang gi blta byar gyur pa'i chu klung dang , longs spyod byar gyur pa'i chu klung bskams pa yod de, 'gro ba gsum gyis brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe na, las kyi dbang gis rnag khrag sogs dngos po rnam pa gsum cig car du grub pa zhig yod pa'i phyir
record.english: From one point of view, the river of water hasn't dried up when the craving spirit looks at it; but there is a river which has dried up, if you're talking about a river of water that the spirit can see, or a river of water that the spirit can drink from. This follows because when the three different types of beings sit down together and look at a glass full of something wet and flowing, it is true that, due to the force of karma, three different kinds of objects exist there at the same time: the pus and blood, and the other two.

record.acip: BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA LHA MI YI DVAGS DUD 'GRO SOGS KYIS CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA, LHA YI BDUD RTZI SNANG BA'I SNANG BA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA DANG , YI DVAGS LA RNAG KHRAG SNANG BA'I SNANG BA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA YOD KYANG , SNANG GZHIR GYUR PA'I RNAG KHRAG SOGS MED NA, SEMS CAN DMYAL BA'I MIG SHES DES, DMYAL BA'I LCAGS SREG DANG , RAL GRI'I NAGS TSAL DANG , ME TSOGS LA SOGS PA SNANG BA'I SNANG BA TZAM LA TSAD MAR SONG BA YOD KYI, DE DAG DNGOS GNAS PA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA MED PAR THAL, KHYOD KYI DAM BCA' 'THAD PA GANG ZHIG, RGYU MTSAN MTSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
record.wylie: brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la lha mi yi dvags dud 'gro sogs kyis cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe na, lha yi bdud rtsi snang ba'i snang ba la tshad mar song ba dang , yi dvags la rnag khrag snang ba'i snang ba la tshad mar song ba yod kyang , snang gzhir gyur pa'i rnag khrag sogs med na, sems can dmyal ba'i mig shes des, dmyal ba'i lcags sreg dang , ral gri'i nags tshal dang , me tshogs la sogs pa snang ba'i snang ba tsam la tshad mar song ba yod kyi, de dag dngos gnas pa la tshad mar song ba med par thal, khyod kyi dam bca' 'thad pa gang zhig, rgyu mtshan mtshungs pa'i phyir
record.english: And consider again this case where a pleasure being and a human and a craving spirit and an animal or the like all sit down together and look at a glass full of something wet and flowing. According to you, it would have to be genuine when something that just looked like ambrosia appeared to the pleasure being, and it would have to be genuine when something that just looked like pus and blood appeared to the craving spirit, but there couldn't be any pus and blood out there to appear as pus and blood. And if this were the case, then consider the visual consciousness of a being in the hells. It would then have to be a valid perception towards something appearing to it that just looked like the burning steel of the hells, and towards something that just looked like the forest of swords, and towards something that just looked like a mass of fire, and so on. Finally, this person would not have any valid perceptions at all towards any of these things as actual objects. Why would this all have to be so? If your idea were correct, it would have to be, for the logic here is identical to your own.

record.acip: 'DOD NA, LCAGS SREG LA SOGS PAS, DER SKYES PA'I 'GRO BA'I LUS SREG PA DANG , GTUB PA LA SOGS PA DNGOS GNAS PA ZHIG MED PAR THAL, 'DOD PA DE'I PHYIR, 'DOD NA, DMYAL BA'I SDUG BSNGAL MED PAR THAL, 'DOD PA DE'I PHYIR, GZHAN YANG DE LTAR CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA, MI'I MIG SHES TSAD MAR SONG BA'I CHU DNGOS GNAS PA MED PAR THAL, DE'I TSE NA RNAG KHRAG DNGOS GNAS PA MED PA'I PHYIR,
record.wylie: 'dod na, lcags sreg la sogs pas, der skyes pa'i 'gro ba'i lus sreg pa dang , gtub pa la sogs pa dngos gnas pa zhig med par thal, 'dod pa de'i phyir, 'dod na, dmyal ba'i sdug bsngal med par thal, 'dod pa de'i phyir, gzhan yang de ltar cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe na, mi'i mig shes tshad mar song ba'i chu dngos gnas pa med par thal, de'i tshe na rnag khrag dngos gnas pa med pa'i phyir
record.english: And suppose you agree that this hell being could have no valid perceptions of the type we mentioned. Well then, the burning steel and other objects could never perform any real actions: they could never burn the bodies of the people born there, they could never chop them up, and so on. Why? Well because of what you just agreed to. And suppose you agree to this; that they could never perform any real actions. Well then, the torment of the hells itself then must not even exist, by your own admission. And remember too that case where the beings all sit down and look at the same thing. You must be saying then that the actual water, the thing towards which the visual consciousness of the human is a valid perception, doesn't exist at all. Why? Well because, according to you, no actual pus and blood exists either in the same situation.

record.acip: KHO NA RE, DE'I TSE NA CHU DNGOS GNAS PA YOD DE, CHUS LUS 'KHRUD PA DANG 'TSOD PAR BYED PA MI RANG GIS MYONG BAS 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR ZER NA, 'O NA, DE'I TSE NA, RNAG KHRAG DNGOS GNAS YOD PAR THAL, DE'I TSE NA, RNAG KHRAG LA LONGS SPYOD PA DANG , LTO BA DANG MGRIN PA LA SOGS PA 'TSIG PA YI DVAGS RANG GIS MYONG BAS 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR,
record.wylie: kho na re, de'i tshe na chu dngos gnas pa yod de, chus lus 'khrud pa dang 'tshod par byed pa mi rang gis myong bas 'grub pa'i phyir zer na, 'o na, de'i tshe na, rnag khrag dngos gnas yod par thal, de'i tshe na, rnag khrag la longs spyod pa dang , lto ba dang mgrin pa la sogs pa 'tshig pa yi dvags rang gis myong bas 'grub pa'i phyir
record.english: Someone might now make the following claim: In this situation, there does exist some real water there. This is because the human can confirm the water with his own experience, as it performs all the functions of water--as he uses it to wash himself, or as he uses it to cook something. Well then, in the same situation there must exist some real pus and blood there as well, because in this same situation the craving spirit can confirm the pus and blood with his own experience as they perform their functions--as he drinks them, and then as the sizzle in his throat and stomach, and so on.

record.acip: BYAS PA LA KHO NA RE, MI LA LUS 'KHRUD PA SOGS DNGOS GNAS PA MED PAR THAL, DE MI RANG GI BLOS RLOM PA TZAM YIN PA'I PHYIR, ZER NA,
record.wylie: byas pa la kho na re, mi la lus 'khrud pa sogs dngos gnas pa med par thal, de mi rang gi blos rlom pa tsam yin pa'i phyir, zer na
record.english: Someone may respond to this with another claim: When the human washes himself with the water and so on, it must not be something real, because it's nothing more than his own imagination.

record.acip: YI DVAGS LA YANG LTO BSREG PA SOGS DNGOS GNAS PA MED PAR THAL, DE YI DVAGS RANG GI BLOS RLOM PA TZAM YIN PA'I PHYIR, 'DOD NA, YI DVAGS KYI SDUG BSNGAL MED PAR THAL,
record.wylie: yi dvags la yang lto bsreg pa sogs dngos gnas pa med par thal, de yi dvags rang gi blos rlom pa tsam yin pa'i phyir, 'dod na, yi dvags kyi sdug bsngal med par thal
record.english: Are you saying then that when the pus and blood sizzle in the stomach of the craving spirit, and so on, it can't be something real? For that too is nothing more than his own imagination. You agree? Well then, the suffering of craving spirits must not exist at all.

record.acip: KHO NA RE, DE LTAR CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA'I TSE, RNAG KHRAG DNGOS GNAS PA MED PAR THAL, RAB RIB CAN GYIS BSE RU LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE BSE RU'I NANG DU SKRA SHAD MED PA GANG ZHIG, RAB RIB DANG LDAN DBANG PO CAN MTSUNGS PA, , CHU 'BAB KLUNG LA YI DVAGS RNAG BLO YANG , , ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR, ZER NA,
record.wylie: kho na re, de ltar cig car du bltas pa'i tshe, rnag khrag dngos gnas pa med par thal, rab rib can gyis bse ru la bltas pa de'i tshe bse ru'i nang du skra shad med pa gang zhig, rab rib dang ldan dbang po can mtshungs pa, , chu 'bab klung la yi dvags rnag blo yang , , zhes gsungs pa'i phyir, zer na
record.english: Someone might make the following claim: Isn't it true that when all those beings sit down together and look at something, there isn't any actual pus and blood at all? Because isn't it true first of all that, when a person with cataracts looks into a porcelain basin, there is no strand of hair in the basin at all? And, secondly, doesn't [Master Dharmakirti's] text itself say, Identical to the case of someone where his sense power has a cataract, Is the mind of a craving spirit as well, which sees a stream of water as pus.

record.acip: SKYON MED DE, DBU SEMS GNYIS DON SHES YOD MED MTSUNGS MI MTSUNGS DPYOD PA'I SKABS YIN PA'I PHYIR DANG , YI DVAGS KYI MIG SHES LA CHU KLUNG RNAG KHRAG TU SNANG BA'I TSE NA, DE LTAR SNANG BA'I MIG SHES TSAD MA MA YIN PA DANG , CHU KLUNG LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA, RNAG KHRAG DNGOS GNAS PA ZHIG YOD PA MI 'GAL BA'I PHYIR,
record.wylie: skyon med de, dbu sems gnyis don shes yod med mtshungs mi mtshungs dpyod pa'i skabs yin pa'i phyir dang , yi dvags kyi mig shes la chu klung rnag khrag tu snang ba'i tshe na, de ltar snang ba'i mig shes tshad ma ma yin pa dang , chu klung la bltas pa de'i tshe na, rnag khrag dngos gnas pa zhig yod pa mi 'gal ba'i phyir
record.english: And yet there is no such problem, for this quotation appears in the section where we are examining the question of whether, in the schools of the Middle Way and the Mind-Only, an object and the perception of it must be equivalent in either both existing or both not existing. Moreover, there is another fact about this situation, where the stream of water appears as pus and blood to the visual consciousness of the craving spirit. It is no inconsistency to say that the visual consciousness that sees things this way is not a valid perception, and to say at the same time that--when the craving spirit looks at the stream of water--there does exist there actual pus and blood.

record.acip: YANG KHA CIG, 'GRO BA GSUM GYIS BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA'I TSE NA, RNAG KHRAG DNGOS GNAS PA MED PAR THAL, DMYAL BA'I LCAGS SREG LA SOGS PA DER SKYES PA'I SEMS CAN GYI SNANG BA TZAM YIN GYI, DNGOS GNAS SU GRUB PA MED PA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, DE 'DRA'I BYED PA PO SU YANG MED PA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, SPYOD 'JUG LAS, LCAGS SREG SA GZHI SU YIS BYAS, , ME TSOGS DE DAG CI LAS BYUNG , , DE 'DRA DE DAG THAMS CAD KYANG , SDIG SEMS YIN PAR THUB PAS GSUNGS, , ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR, ZER NA,
record.wylie: yang kha cig, 'gro ba gsum gyis brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la cig car du bltas pa'i tshe na, rnag khrag dngos gnas pa med par thal, dmyal ba'i lcags sreg la sogs pa der skyes pa'i sems can gyi snang ba tsam yin gyi, dngos gnas su grub pa med pa'i phyir, der thal, de 'dra'i byed pa po su yang med pa'i phyir, der thal, spyod 'jug las, lcags sreg sa gzhi su yis byas, , me tshogs de dag ci las byung , , de 'dra de dag thams cad kyang , sdig sems yin par thub pas gsungs, , zhes gsungs pa'i phyir, zer na
record.english: Someone again may come and claim the following: Let's consider once more this situation where three different types of beings sit down together and look at a glass full of something wet and flowing. Isn't it true that there is no actual pus and blood there? Because isn't it true that the burning steel and so on in the hells is only something that appears to a person who is born there, but that there is nothing there which actually is these objects? Because isn't it true that there is no one at all who went and made all these kinds of things? And isn't this a fact, because doesn't the text of The Bodhisattva's Way of Life say: Who made the burning steel that acts As the floor of the world of hell? Where did all the mass of flames You find there all come from? The Able Ones have spoken that Everything there like this Is nothing at all other than The mind of what's non-virtue.

record.acip: BZHI DGE SLONG 'CHAR KA LTA BU LA TSANG BA LAS, MGON PO KLU SGRUB LA'ANG DNGOS GNAS PA MTSANG LA, RANG RES KYANG SANGS RGYAS DANG KHYAD MED PA'I BLA MA MJAL TE CHOS GSUNGS PA SOGS KYIS DE DAG DOD THUB SBYOR DU YOD PA LAS DNGOS GNAS MA TSANG YANG , DAL BA BRGYAD DNGOS SU TSANG BA LA GTZO BOR DGONGS TE GSUNGS PA RED,
record.wylie: bzhi dge slong 'char ka lta bu la tshang ba las, mgon po klu sgrub la'ang dngos gnas pa mtshang la, rang res kyang sangs rgyas dang khyad med pa'i bla ma mjal te chos gsungs pa sogs kyis de dag dod thub sbyor du yod pa las dngos gnas ma tshang yang , dal ba brgyad dngos su tshang ba la gtso bor dgongs te gsungs pa red
record.english: All four of the fortunes just explained have been possessed even by the likes of the monk Udayi, whereas the same cannot be said even for the Savior Nagarjuna, who lacked them in their literal form. We too have met our Lamas, who are no different from a Buddha, and they have spoken the Dharma and so on; these are a full substitute yes, but we cannot say that we have all those fortunes in their literal form. We do however enjoy all eight of the spiritual leisures; these then are our primary advantage, and it's with this fact in mind that the verse reads "life of leisure."

Where did all the mass of flames You find there all come from? The Able Ones have spoken that Everything there like this Is nothing at all other than The mind of what's non-virtue.

record.acip: DE LA NI SPYOD PA MI DGOS KYANG SEMS DBEN GYI TING NGE 'DZIN LA GOMS PAR BYAS PAS TSE 'DIR LUS GNYIS SO SOR 'BYED PA DANG , PHYE BA'I LUS DE SGYU LUS RDO RJE 'CHANG GI SKUR DNGOS GNAS PAR LDANG BA NI SHIN TU BSGRUB BKA' BAS SNGON DU SPYOD PA GSUM GANG RUNG NGES PAR BYA DGOS PAR GSUNGS SO,,
record.wylie: de la ni spyod pa mi dgos kyang sems dben gyi ting nge 'dzin la goms par byas pas tshe 'dir lus gnyis so sor 'byed pa dang , phye ba'i lus de sgyu lus rdo rje 'chang gi skur dngos gnas par ldang ba ni shin tu bsgrub bka' bas sngon du spyod pa gsum gang rung nges par bya dgos par gsungs so
record.english: Even though none of the activities is necessary here, it is nonetheless extremely difficult to use continued practice in the one-point concentration of transcendent mind to separate the two bodies from each other here in this life; and to rise up in the actual illusory body: in the body of the Keeper of the Diamond himself.  As such, it is stated that we must absolutely engage in one or more of the three activities.

record.acip: SNGAGS BLA MED KYI LAM LNGA DANG SA BCU DNGOS GNAS PA NI GSAL SGRON LAS, LAM THUN MONG BA NAS BZUNG STE, BSGOMS STOBS KYIS RLUNG DH'U T'IR BTZUD PA THIM PAS STONG PA DNGOS SU 'DREN MI NUS PA DE SRID DU TSOGS KYI LAM DANG ,
record.wylie: sngags bla med kyi lam lnga dang sa bcu dngos gnas pa ni gsal sgron las, lam thun mong ba nas bzung ste, bsgoms stobs kyis rlung dhU tIr btsud pa thim pas stong pa dngos su 'dren mi nus pa de srid du tshogs kyi lam dang
record.english: The real five paths and ten levels in the unsurpassed teachings are those described as follows in the Lantern-- The path of accumulation goes from the point where you are on the shared path on up to the point where you are just about to become able to use your meditation to get the winds into the channel of dance, and thereby bring on an experience of emptiness in a direct way.

record.acip: ZHES STONG GZUGS KYI SKU DNGOS GNAS PA 'GRUB PA LA BEMS PO'I KHAMS ZAD DGOS PAR GSUNGS PA GNYIS MI 'GAL TSUL JI LTAR YIN, STONG GZUGS KYI LHA SKU DNGOS GNAS LA 'GRUB PA'I MTSAMS GANG NAS YIN,
record.wylie: zhes stong gzugs kyi sku dngos gnas pa 'grub pa la bems po'i khams zad dgos par gsungs pa gnyis mi 'gal tshul ji ltar yin, stong gzugs kyi lha sku dngos gnas la 'grub pa'i mtshams gang nas yin
record.english: What this last is saying then is that, in order to attain the actual form of the holy body of empty form, we must bring all the various material parts of us to an end.  How then is it that these two presentations aren't in contradiction with each other?  And at which point is it, exactly, that we do attain the actual form of the Angel's holy body of empty form?

record.acip: DANG PO NI, RANG GI PHUNG PO LNGA DANG, KHAMS BCO BRGYAD, SKYE MCHED BCU GNYIS, KUN RTOG BRGYAD CU MA DAG 'KHOR BA'I GNAS RNAMS RGYA CHE,
record.wylie: dang po ni, rang gi phung po lnga dang, khams bco brgyad, skye mched bcu gnyis, kun rtog brgyad cu ma dag 'khor ba'i gnas rnams rgya che
record.english: The extensive thing which you must purify is the impure nature of your suffering body and mind. This is made up of the five heaps, the eighteen categories, the twelve doors of perception, and the eighty different kinds of conceptions.

record.acip: LAM GYI SKABS SKYE SHI BAR DO GSUM LA RNAL 'BYOR PAS SANGS RGYAS KYI SKU GSUM DE DANG CHA MTHUN PA TZAM LA SKU GSUM GYI THA SNYAD BYED KYANG SKU GSUM DNGOS GNAS PA NI MIN GSUNGS,
record.wylie: lam gyi skabs skye shi bar do gsum la rnal 'byor pas sangs rgyas kyi sku gsum de dang cha mthun pa tsam la sku gsum gyi tha snyad byed kyang sku gsum dngos gnas pa ni min gsungs
record.english: What happens while the secret practitioner is still on the path, said our Lama, is that he or she refers to birth, death, and the state between death and birth as the "Three Bodies," but only by way of simile.  They are not at that point the actual Three.

record.acip: DE NAS DNGOS SAM YE SHES KYI PHYAG RGYA MDUN DU BSAMS LA, BDAG DANG PHYAG RGYA GNYIS KA'I 'OG TU YAm LAS RLUNG, STENG DU RAm LAS ME, RLUNG GIS ME SBAR BAS THA MAL BA'I MA DAG PA'I PHUNG PO KHAMS DANG SKYE MCHED THAMS CAD BSREGS TE STONG PAR BSAM,
record.wylie: de nas dngos sam ye shes kyi phyag rgya mdun du bsams la, bdag dang phyag rgya gnyis ka'i 'og tu yaM las rlung, steng du raM las me, rlung gis me sbar bas tha mal ba'i ma dag pa'i phung po khams dang skye mched thams cad bsregs te stong par bsam
record.english: Then again bring before you either your actual partner; or an imaginary one, in your mind.  See below yourself and your partner an yam syllable; from it comes wind.  Above it is a ram syllable, and from this comes fire.  The wind whips up the fire, and it burns up all your impure heaps and categories and doors of perception--the normal ones.  Think then that it has all gone into emptiness.

record.acip: DE LTAR GNAS TSOD LA RMI LAM DU SHAR BA RNAMS DON DE DNGOS GNAS PA MA YIN KYANG, DE LTA NA'ANG BDE SDUG DU MA ZHIG (RMI LAM) GYI TSE LA SKYED PA (JI) LTA BA DE (BZHIN) DU BDEN PAR MED KYANG KUN RDZOB TZAM DU SO SO (SKYE) BO RNAMS DANG, ('PHAGS) PA'I GANG ZAG (THAMS CAD KYI) RGYUD LA (BDE BA) DANG (DGA') BA'I KHYAD PAR SNA TSOGS PA (CI YANG 'CHAR BA) STE 'BYUNG BA('I)
record.wylie: de ltar gnas tshod la rmi lam du shar ba rnams don de dngos gnas pa ma yin kyang, de lta na'ang bde sdug du ma zhig (rmi lam) gyi tshe la skyed pa (ji) lta ba de (bzhin) du bden par med kyang kun rdzob tsam du so so (skye) bo rnams dang, ('phags) pa'i gang zag (thams cad kyi) rgyud la (bde ba) dang (dga') ba'i khyad par sna tshogs pa (ci yang 'char ba) ste 'byung ba('i)
record.english: And so in actual fact, none of the objects which appear to us in a dream is the real thing; but when we're having a dream lots of feelings of pleasure or pain can still come up.  Here with our rejoicing it's just the same.  Both those individuals who are normal people and those who have experienced emptiness do all directly experience or undergo in their hearts a variety of sensations which are pleasure and happiness, even though none of these feelings exists in reality, but rather only in a deceptive manner--that is, if only in a way which resembles the way these come in a dream.

record.acip: DE YANG 'PHO BA NAS RAB TU BYUNG BA MA MDZAD KYI BAR DU KHYIM PA DANG, DE PHYIN CHAD NI RAB TU BYUNG BA DANG, MDZAD PA YANG DE DANG BSTUN NAS, KHYIM PA DANG RAB BYUNG GI MDZAD PA YANG DNGOS GNAS PAR 'DOD,

record.english: The Detailists also say that—from the time that he moved, up to the time that he took ordination in this world—Lord Buddha was a householder.  From that point on, he lived as an ordained person.  This idea is reflected in their version of the Buddha's deeds, where they see the householder and the ordained deeds as what was actually going on.

record.english: The Detailists, for example, would say that existing entities which were not produced by causes & conditions—as well as things like partless atoms—are part of ultimate reality; whereas the Sutrists would assign these to deceptive reality.  And the Detailists would say that form which does not inform us of a person's intent is actual physical form—whereas our other system would say that it was just “physical form” in name. record.english: The autocommentary to The Twenty Verses cites the same lines of the sutra, and says that the word “mind” here is intended to include those items which share a mental link with main mind. And then it states that the term “only” here is meant to deny the object.

record.english: Now at the very end you should look into yourself and see whether things really happened the way you pictured they should when you did the giving and taking. And what you will find is that it was all only a wish: that in actuality there was no help or happiness which came about at present. This should lead you to think to yourself, "Well then, I will have to see to it that this actually does happen." Try to bring up in your heart therefore the feeling of personal responsibility, where you decide that you would be willing to carry the load all on your own. record.acip: ZER NA MA KHYAB STE DANG POR YI DWAGS KYIS CHU MA MTHONG NA PHYOGS DER LONGS SPYOD, PA'I PHYIR 'GRO BA YANG MI 'THAD PAS DANG POR CHU MTHONG YANG PHYIS LAS KYI DBANG, GIS CHU MA MTHONG BAR 'OG GZHI GRAM SREG TZAM ZHIG MTHONG ZHING DE'I RJES SU RTOG, PAS CHU BSKAMS PAR ZHEN PA DANG DE BZHIN DU DANG POR LJON SHING GI 'BRAS BU MTHONG YANG PHYIS LAS KYI DBANG GIS 'BRAS BU MA MTHONG BAR YAL GA TZAM ZHIG MTHONG ZHING DE'I RJES SU RTOG PAS 'BRAS BU MED PAR ZHEN PA'I PHYIR

record.english: Just because we said that about the other case doesn't mean that it's true in every case. If the craving spirit hadn't seen any water in that area in the first place, it wouldn't have made any sense for him to go over in that direction to try to enjoy some of the water. Therefore what happened was that, at first, he saw some water. Later on, he was forced by his karma to stop seeing water and saw only bare, parched earth. Then he had an impression where he thought the water had dried up. The case with the fruit tree is the same. Although at first the craving spirit sees a tree loaded with fruit, later on his karma forces him to stop seeing fruit, and all he sees is bare branches. Then he has an impression where he thinks that the tree has no fruit any more.

record.acip: RNAM PA GCIG TU NA YI DWAGS KYIS CHU KLUNG LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA DE MA BSKAMS, KYANG RANG GI BLTA BYAR GYUR PA'I CHU KLUNG DANG LONGS SPYOD BYAR GYUR PA'I CHU KLUNG BSKAMS PA YOD DE 'GRO BA GSUM GYIS BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA CIG, CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA LAS KYI DBANG GIS RNAG KHRAG SOGS DNGOS PO RNAM PA, GSUM CIG CAR DU GRUB PA ZHIG YOD PA'I PHYIR

record.english: From one point of view, the river of water hasn't dried up when the craving spirit looks at it; but there is a river which has dried up, if you're talking about a river of water that the spirit can see, or a river of water that the spirit can drink from. This follows because when the three different types of beings sit down together and look at a glass full of something wet and flowing, it is true that, due to the force of karma, three different kinds of objects exist there at the same time: the pus and blood, and the other two.

record.acip: BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA LHA MI YI DWAGS DUD 'GRO SOGS KYIS CIG CAR DU, BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA LHA YI BDUD RTZI SNANG BA'I SNANG BA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA DANG YI DWAGS LA RNAG KHRAG SNANG BA'I SNANG BA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA YOD KYANG SNANG GZHIR GYUR PA'I RNAG KHRAG SOGS MED NA SEMS CAN DMYAL BA'I MIG SHES DES DMYAL BA'I LCAGS SREG DANG RAL GRI'I NAGS TSAL DANG ME TSOGS LA SOGS PA SNANG BA'I SNANG BA TZAM LA TSAD MAR SONG BA YOD KYI DE DAG DNGOS GNAS PA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA MED PAR THAL KHYOD KYI DAM BCA' 'THAD PA GANG ZHIG RGYU MTSAN MTSUNGS PA'I PHYIR
record.wylie: brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la lha mi yi dwags dud 'gro sogs kyis cig car du, bltas pa de'i tshe na lha yi bdud rtsi snang ba'i snang ba la tshad mar song ba dang yi dwags la rnag khrag snang ba'i snang ba la tshad mar song ba yod kyang snang gzhir gyur pa'i rnag khrag sogs med na sems can dmyal ba'i mig shes des dmyal ba'i lcags sreg dang ral gri'i nags tshal dang me tshogs la sogs pa snang ba'i snang ba tsam la tshad mar song ba yod kyi de dag dngos gnas pa la tshad mar song ba med par thal khyod kyi dam bca' 'thad pa gang zhig rgyu mtshan mtshungs pa'i phyir
record.english: And consider again this case where a pleasure being and a human and a craving spirit and an animal or the like all sit down together and look at a glass full of something wet and flowing. According to you, it would have to be genuine when something that just looked like ambrosia appeared to the pleasure being, and it would have to be genuine when something that just looked like pus and blood appeared to the craving spirit, but there couldn't be any pus and blood out there to appear as pus and blood. And if this were the case, then consider the visual consciousness of a being in the hells. It would then have to be a valid perception towards something appearing to it that just looked like the burning steel of the hells, and towards something that just looked like the forest of swords, and towards something that just looked like a mass of fire, and so on. Finally, this person would not have any valid perceptions at all towards any of these things as actual objects. Why would this all have to be so? If your idea were correct, it would have to be, for the logic here is identical to your own.

record.wylie: kho na re de'i tshe na chu dngos gnas pa yod de chus lus 'khrud pa dang 'tshod par, byed pa mi rang gis myong bas 'grub pa'i phyir zer na 'o na de'i tshe na rnag khrag dngos gnas yod par thal de'i tshe na rnag khrag la longs spyod pa dang lto ba dang mgrin pa la sogs pa 'tshig pa yi dwags rang gis myong bas 'grub pa'i phyir
record.english: Someone might now make the following claim: In this situation, there does exist some real water there. This is because the human can confirm the water with his own experience, as it performs all the functions of water—as he uses it to wash himself, or as he uses it to cook something. Well then, in the same situation there must exist some real pus and blood there as well, because in this same situation the craving spirit can confirm the pus and blood with his own experience as they perform their functions—as he drinks them, and then as the sizzle in his throat and stomach, and so on.

record.english: Are you saying then that when the pus and blood sizzle in the stomach of the craving spirit, and so on, it can't be something real? For that too is nothing more than his own imagination. You agree? Well then, the suffering of craving spirits must not exist at all.

record.english: Someone might make the following claim: Isn't it true that when all those beings sit down together and look at something, there isn't any actual pus and blood at all? Because isn't it true first of all that, when a person with cataracts looks into a porcelain basin, there is no strand of hair in the basin at all? And, secondly, doesn't [Master Dharmakirti's] text itself say, Identical to the case of someone where his sense power has a cataract, Is the mind of a craving spirit as well, which sees a stream of water as pus.

record.wylie: skyon med de dbu sems gnyis don shes yod med mtshungs mi mtshungs dpyod pa'i, skabs yin pa'i phyir dang yi dwags kyi mig shes la chu klung rnag khrag tu snang ba'i tshe na de ltar snang ba'i mig shes tshad ma ma yin pa dang chu klung la bltas pa de'i tshe na rnag khrag dngos gnas pa zhig yod pa mi 'gal ba'i phyir
record.english: And yet there is no such problem, for this quotation appears in the section where we are examining the question of whether, in the schools of the Middle Way and the Mind-Only, an object and the perception of it must be equivalent in either both existing or both not existing. Moreover, there is another fact about this situation, where the stream of water appears as pus and blood to the visual consciousness of the craving spirit. It is no inconsistency to say that the visual consciousness that sees things this way is not a valid perception, and to say at the same time that—when the craving spirit looks at the stream of water—there does exist there actual pus and blood.

record.english: And that's true because-in that system-whenever any state of mind is an accurate perception towards the eye or such, then it must always be because it has constituted an accurate perception towards the eye and so forth as a specific expression.
